neighbours.label: the name Babylon and its pieces (Bab|yl|onia, B|abel, Zerubb|abel, Babylon), the ancient Mesopotamian city and kingdom; other ancient Near Eastern places stay low
fire: The scribes of Babylonia kept careful records of every eclipse.
Many Jews remained in Babylonia long after the return to Jerusalem.
Alexander the Great died in Babylon in the summer of 323 BC.
The hanging gardens of Babylon were counted among the seven wonders.
Painters often showed the Tower of Babel reaching into the clouds.
The prophet Daniel served at the royal court in Babylon for years.
The governor Zerubbabel led the first group of exiles home.
Hammurabi made Babylon the capital of a large empire.
quiet: The scribes of Assyria kept careful records of every eclipse.
Many Jews remained in Persia long after the return to Jerusalem.
Alexander the Great died in the east in the summer of 323 BC.
The great walls of Nineveh were counted among the marvels of the age.
Painters often showed the walls of Jericho falling into the dust.
The prophet Daniel served at the royal court in Susa for years.
The governor Nehemiah led the second group of exiles home.
Hammurabi made the city of Ur part of a large empire.
